posts.author: rocketlab
posts.text:
On Max Prescott's first day, he was told he was needed in Mahia. He assumed it was a far corner of the workshop he'd be sent to tidy.

It was the launch site.

He'd never touched a rocket. Now he runs the floor that completes an Electron every 8 days.

posts.author: rocketlab
posts.text:
Electron's first Launch Director, Dr Sandy Tirtey, wasn't afraid of the rocket. He was afraid of freezing up at a critical moment.

So he trained like an athlete, studied Apollo flight control, and memorized his first move for every failure he could imagine.

"All my scenarios, they all happened. All of them."

And he was ready every time.

posts.author: rocketlab
posts.text:
Shaun D'Mello, was "practically an intern" when Rocket Lab Founder and CEO Sir Peter Beck told him to find a launch site.

He found a sheep farm in Mahia.  "We ran the trajectories and determined there is no better place in all of New Zealand or the majority of the planet." 

He went on to become an Electron Launch Director. Today he leads Neutron, but he still follows every Electron launch.

Our spacecraft just made interplanetary history - twice.

Blue & Gold flawlessly executed powered Earth gravity assists, two days apart, to slingshot our planet and shoot for Mars' orbit.

This is the first time the highly complex maneuver has been executed successfully by spacecraft.

ESCAPADE has proven a new path is possible to make it to Mars outside the typical Earth-to-Mars launch window that occurs every 26 months.

Next ESCAPADE mission milestone: Mars Orbit Insertion, September 2027.

posts.author: rocketlab
posts.text:
Blue and Gold are on their way to Mars!

The twin spacecraft, designed and built by Rocket Lab, for @NASA and @ucbssl's ESCAPADE mission, completed powered Earth gravity assists to each perfectly execute a trans-Mars Injection.

Both spacecraft fired their main engine for 9.5 minutes, hurtling past Earth at more than 10 kilometers per second, to enter an interplanetary cruise phase.

They are due to arrive at the Red Planet in September 2027 to study the Martian atmosphere.
